comments.body:
## RCA — Phase 1 complete (rebar-debug)

**Classification: `defect`** (an **omission**, not a regression — the returncode check was never
written at either site; there is no good→bad transition to bisect).

### Proven mechanism

Both named sites derive their *entire* verdict from the absence of a string in a real child's
captured output, and never consult `returncode`. A child killed by a signal is torn down by the
kernel before it writes, so `stdout == stderr == ""`, the substring is trivially absent, and the
oracle reports GREEN for a run that never executed.

The changeable artifacts:

- `tests/unit/test_git_floor_gate_tree_skew.py:127` —
  `assert "::error::" not in (result.stdout + result.stderr)`, the whole body of
  `test_absent_floor_file_emits_no_workflow_error`. `_run_gate` (same file, ~line 54) is a bare
  `subprocess.run([...], capture_output=True)` — no `check=True`, no returncode assertion.
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py:151` —
  `assert "unknown subcommand 'reconcile'" not in (cp.stdout + cp.stderr).lower()`, the sole
  assertion of `test_reconcile_intercepted_dry_run_default`. `_cli` (line 22) likewise never
  checks the returncode.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py:228` and `:242` — `returncode != 0`,
  which a `-9` satisfies, so the returncode check is present but the wrong shape.

### Proof (discriminating experiments, both run)

**Experiment A — the oracle expressions, against a real killed child.** A child running
`os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGKILL)` was spawned for real (not a hand-built
`CompletedProcess`). Observed: `returncode=-9  stdout=''  stderr=''`. Feeding that into each of
the three assertion expressions verbatim:

```
SITE 1 ORACLE: PASSES (GREEN) on a signal-killed child  <-- FAIL-OPEN
SITE 2 ORACLE: PASSES (GREEN) on a signal-killed child  <-- FAIL-OPEN
SITE 3 ORACLE (returncode != 0): PASSES on a signal-killed child <-- does not close the gap
```

**Experiment B — the real test bodies, driven under pytest.** `subprocess.run` was monkeypatched
inside each test module to spawn the suicide child instead of the intended one, and the *actual*
test functions were invoked. pytest reported **2 passed**:

```
SITE1: real test body PASSED against a child that never ran
SITE2: real test body PASSED against a child that never ran
```

Experiment B is the discriminating one: A alone could be dismissed as a statement about a
substring, B shows the shipped test functions themselves report green when the thing they guard
never ran. It also rules out the rival explanation that some fixture, `conftest`, or helper
already asserts the child's exit — nothing intercepted the killed child anywhere in either call
chain.

### Authoritative source the behaviour violates

- Closed bug `f0fb-de7a-b315-4508` and closed bug `0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e` (`plan_defect`) — the
  same construct class was adjudicated a defect twice and fixed in `tests/e2e` and the live-DC
  tier respectively.
- The design invariant is written down in-repo: `tests/_child_diag.py:56-79`,
  `assert_child_ran_clean`'s docstring — *"WHY the returncode is checked AT ALL, and why FIRST …
  That is a fail-OPEN … the returncode is therefore checked BEFORE the traceback."*

### Attribution — omission, by scope-of-work (three origins, one per site)

There is no introducing commit that *broke* working behaviour; line-scoped `git blame -w -C -M`
on the assertion lines lands on the commits that first authored them, each of which shipped the
oracle already fail-open. Attribution is therefore by scope-of-work, per the omission case.

| Site | blame (line-scoped) | date | origin ticket |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — `test_git_floor_gate_tree_skew.py:127` | `c4c4e1782db` | 2026-08-04 | **`7e90-233b-3ee9-4f14`** (`rebar-ticket:` trailer) |
| 2 — `test_cli.py:151` | `04117bd74a8` | 2026-06-08 | **no ticket** — pre-trailer-convention commit |
| 3 — `test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py:228,242` | `8593a7e7cb9` | 2026-08-12 | **`8aed-e264-7112-4c2f`** (`rebar-ticket:` trailer) |

`caused_by` is recorded against `7e90-233b-3ee9-4f14` — site 1 is the primary site (a
*success/health* oracle, the dangerous direction) and its commit authored the whole test
including its sole assertion, so a reviewer of that change could plausibly have caught it.
`8aed-e264-7112-4c2f` is recorded as a second `caused_by` for site 3.

**Site 2 is unattributable to a ticket, and here is the search.** `git log -S"unknown subcommand
'reconcile'"` over `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py` (and its pre-move path
`tests/interfaces/test_cli.py`) returns exactly one commit, `04117bd74a8` (2026-06-08); it
carries neither a `rebar-ticket:` trailer nor a leading `<id>:` subject, predating that
convention. The later commit that rewrote the surrounding test body — `914891b016a`
(2026-06-11, ticket `e4c3-757a-161b-48c3`) — is deliberately **not** named: blame shows it did
not touch line 151, and naming it would be blaming the most recent toucher rather than the
origin.

**Divergence from the blame default, stated explicitly.** A whole-file blame majority on either
file would name a much more recent toucher (the files have been edited many times since). The
line-scoped blame above is what produced these three, and it disagrees with that default.

**Why the origins are NOT `f0fb` / `0e1d`.** The tempting "unmet obligation" reading — those
tickets created the *"a child-output oracle must check the returncode first"* contract and these
sites were never updated to it — was considered and rejected on dates. `tests/_child_diag.py`
was created 2026-08-20, *after* all three sites existed, so no site could have been updated to a
contract that did not yet exist. And `0e1d` did not ship past its consumers: its Step-7 sweep is
what filed **this** ticket (`discovered_from 0e1d`). That is the opposite of a defect escape,
and charging it would corrupt the metric it feeds.

### Caller-dependency gate

Cleared in one look — the change is confined to three test functions. Nothing imports or calls
them; the only shared artifact touched is `tests/_child_diag.py`, which is imported (read-only,
no signature change planned) by `tests/e2e/conftest.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_dc_pass_health.py`,
and the live-DC tier.

### Scope note

Restoration only. The fix makes each oracle *honest about when it cannot conclude* — asserting
the child ran to completion before trusting an absence derived from its output. It does not
widen what any oracle asserts about the product.

## Phase 2 — verification record (RED→GREEN, kill matrix, and the 128+N boundary)

### The instrument lied first — worth recording

The FIRST kill-matrix run reported **all five mutations surviving**. That was not the oracle;
it was the measuring harness. pytest colorizes its short summary, so the driver's
`grep -c "^FAILED"` never matched — the line really begins with an ANSI escape, not `F`. The
harness therefore reported `0 failed` **whether or not anything failed**.

That is precisely the defect under repair, one layer up: a check whose negative result is
indistinguishable from "the check never ran". Re-run with `--color=no`, every mutation was
killed. Recording it because the failure mode is invisible in a clean-looking final matrix, and
the next person writing a mutation driver will reach for the same grep.

### Kill matrix — 10 seeded, 10 killed, 0 survivors

Axis A — re-introduce the confirmed root cause by deleting each site's guard:

| mutation | RED |
|---|---|
| site 1 guard deleted | `test_git_floor_gate_skip_oracle_…` only |
| site 2 guard deleted | `test_reconcile_routing_oracle_…` only |
| site 3 guard deleted | `test_redispatch_no_warning_oracle_…` only |
| site 4 guard deleted | `test_pandoc_colour_oracle_…` only |
| site 5 guard deleted | `test_actionlint_fail_fast_oracle_…` only |

One-to-one, no cross-talk — the five tests are genuinely independent.

Axis B — the OTHER independent sides, because a test that derives both sides of its assertion
from one place measures that place, not the behaviour:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| B1 shared predicate never fires (`< 0` → `< -9999`) | all 5 RED |
| B2 shared message drops the signal name | all 5 RED (the message assertion is load-bearing) |
| B3 shim stops killing (`exit 0`) | negative control + its 3 sites RED |
| B5 bash-body kill side stops killing | sites 1 and 3 RED |
| B4 shim exits **137** (positive) | sites do NOT catch it — the boundary, made executable |

### The `128 + N` boundary — measured, not argued

Reviewer challenge: if a site's child is spawned through a shell, a real SIGKILL surfaces as
`137` and never as `-9`, so accepting positive codes would leave that site unfixed while a test
asserts it is a deliberate boundary. Checked empirically on each site's real spawn path rather
than reasoned from the call signature.

**1. Which sites spawn directly?** All five. No `shell=True` anywhere in the five files; every
`argv[0]` is the real program — `bash -c` (site 1), `sys.executable` (site 2), `bash <script>`
(site 3), `pandoc` (site 4), `make` (site 5). Sites 1, 3 and 5 do have *grandchildren* (bash
runs commands, make runs `sh`/`curl`); sites 2 and 4 have none.

**2. `-9` or `137`?** Killing the process Python spawned yields **`-9` at all five**:

```
site1  bash killed          rc=-9    output_empty=True
site1  grandchild killed    rc=-9    output_empty=True   (bash execs into it)
site3  bash killed          rc=-9    output_empty=True
site3  grandchild killed    rc=137   output_empty=False
site5  make killed          rc=-9    output_empty=True
site5  recipe child killed  rc=2     output_empty=False
site2  direct child killed  rc=-9    output_empty=True   (no grandchild)
site4  direct child killed  rc=-9    output_empty=True   (no grandchild)
```

No site can *only* report `128 + N`, so none is left unfixed. The measurement also gives a
better reason for the boundary than the one first offered. The original argument was "rejecting
137 would be a widening". The stronger, measured claim: **an empty capture and a positive
returncode never co-occur here.** The fail-open needs an empty capture, and an empty capture at
these sites only ever arrives with a negative returncode, because whatever survives to report a
`128 + N` also writes a diagnostic. When the code is positive the oracle has real output to
inspect and is doing its job. This is now recorded in the regression test's docstring with the
table above.

### Replication

The original report's own repro seam — patching `subprocess.run` globally, independent of the
per-site seams the regression test uses — no longer reproduces at any of the five: each raises
`AssertionError` naming SIGKILL and the site. 5 passed.

### Residual risk

- **Accepted:** the regression test forces each kill through a module-private seam
  (`_gate_script`, `_redispatch_script`, `_pandoc_path`, `_SANE_PATH`, `sys.executable`). A
  rename would break it without behaviour changing. Accepted because `monkeypatch.setattr`
  raises `AttributeError` on a missing attribute — a rename fails LOUDLY rather than silently
  passing, which is the correct direction for this bug class.
- **Accepted:** the "empty capture ⟹ negative returncode" invariant above is measured and
  documented, not asserted by a test. A future change that made a site's shell swallow its own
  diagnostics would silently narrow the guard's coverage. Left as prose rather than adding
  speculative future-proofing to test infrastructure.
- **Observed, fixed in scope:** the five sites now use a bare `from _child_diag import …`, which
  resolves only because the root `tests/conftest.py` puts `tests/` on `sys.path`. This is the
  repo's existing pattern (`_dc_fixtures.py`, `test_dc_mutations.py`), so it was matched rather
  than changed; it does mean these modules are not importable from outside `tests/`.

## Final report — change 1998 (`3f2fba38a5`), pushed for review

**Problem.** Test oracles whose verdict is the ABSENCE of a string in a real child's output
report GREEN when that child is killed by a signal and writes nothing.

**Proven root cause.** Five test functions spawn a real child and never establish it ran.
A signal-killed child is torn down before writing, so `stdout == stderr == ""`, the string is
trivially absent, and a run that never executed passes. Sites: the sole assertion of
`test_absent_floor_file_emits_no_workflow_error`; the sole assertion of
`test_reconcile_intercepted_dry_run_default`; `test_redispatch_requires_both_the_422_…`
(whose `returncode != 0` accepts `-9`); plus two found by the Step-7 sweep —
`test_pandoc_emits_no_color_form` and `test_actionlint_install_fails_fast_on_download_failure`.

**Proof.** The discriminating experiment drove the shipped test bodies (not the assertion
expressions) with a really-SIGKILLed child: pytest reported PASSED where it should have failed.
That ruled out the rival that some fixture or helper already checked the exit — nothing
intercepted the killed child anywhere in any call chain.

**Defect origin.** Omission, by scope-of-work — no commit broke working behaviour.
`caused_by` recorded against `7e90-233b-3ee9-4f14` (site 1, `c4c4e1782db`) and
`8aed-e264-7112-4c2f` (site 3, `8593a7e7cb9`). Site 2 (`04117bd74a8`, 2026-06-08) is
**unattributable to a ticket**: `git log -S"unknown subcommand 'reconcile'"` over the file and
its pre-move path returns exactly that one commit, which predates the trailer convention. The
`f0fb`/`0e1d` "unmet obligation" reading was rejected on the date test.

**Test.** `tests/unit/test_child_oracle_fail_open.py` — legitimately RED first (5 site tests
failing "DID NOT RAISE" while the negative control proved the kill was real), held out from the
fix subagent, GREEN after. **11 mutations seeded, 11 killed, 0 survivors**, on both the fix side
and the kill side.

**Fix.** One narrow helper, `assert_child_was_not_signal_killed`, rejecting only a NEGATIVE
returncode and delegating its message to `child_failure_detail`; one call per site.

**Scope & safety.** Caller sweep cleared in one look (five test functions, nothing calls them).
Diff is **388 insertions, 0 deletions** — no assertion removed or weakened, no new dependency,
no new capability. Restoration: each oracle becomes honest about when it cannot conclude; none
asserts anything new about the product.

**Siblings — Axis 1 (construct sweep).** Swept all of `tests/` for absent-string-over-child-output
with no returncode assertion. Two live hits beyond the ticket's three (pandoc, actionlint), both
fixed in scope. `tests/e2e` and `tests/external/live_jira_dc` excluded — already fixed by `f0fb`
and `0e1d`.

**Siblings — Axis 2 (parity census).** RULE: *a test whose verdict is the absence of a string in
a spawned child's output must first establish the child was not killed by a signal.* Surfaces =
the test tiers that spawn children:

| tier | status |
|---|---|
| `tests/e2e` | HOLDS — `conftest.py:71,113` via `child_failure_detail` (`f0fb`) |
| `tests/external/live_jira_dc` | HOLDS — `assert_child_ran_clean` throughout (`0e1d`) |
| `tests/unit` | was MISSING ×4 → fixed here |
| `tests/interfaces` | was MISSING ×1 → fixed here |
| `tests/integration` | N/A — uses `check=True`, which raises on a signal death |
| dual direction (assert string PRESENT) | N/A — fails CLOSED; an empty capture cannot satisfy it |

**Replication.** The original report's own seam (patching `subprocess.run` globally, independent
of the per-site seams the regression test uses) no longer reproduces at any of the five.

**Verification.** Full suite green (`11950 passed, 44 skipped`). Order-independence checked by
explicit reordering — new test first / last / middle — 82 passed, 1 skipped each; the
"new test first" ordering also proves the recorder's `subprocess.run` patch does not leak, since
all five spawning site files run after it. `make lint` clean with the ratchet at
`new=0 increased=0 stale=0`; `make typecheck` clean (617 files).

**Note for the next debugger.** Four separate times this session a MEASURING instrument
exhibited the very fail-open shape under repair: a colorized `grep "^FAILED"` that reported
"0 failed" unconditionally; a truncated sweep log that read identically to a clean one; an
orphaned `&` subshell reported as finished; and a `pgrep -f "make test"` that matched the
monitor's own command line and waited on itself. Each was caught only by checking the instrument
against a known-positive case. If you are verifying an absence, verify your instrument can still
see a presence.

comments.body:
## Patchset 2 — the CI `-1`, and what it caught

Patchset 1 took `Verified -1`. Two independent causes, one mine.

### Not mine: definition-vs-tree skew (`optionality / clean core wheel`, 47s)

```
ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/interfaces/contracts/test_cli_registry_distribution.py
collected 0 items  ->  exit 4
```

The Gerrit Verified lane takes the workflow DEFINITION from the target branch but checks out
the CHANGE'S tree. `origin/main` had gained both that test file and the `_optionality.yml:114`
line that runs it; my patchset's base predated both. Six changes were reddened by it. Filed as
`anxious-resistant-urson`, and the guard has since landed in change 2002.

Worth naming: that is **the same bug class as `7e90-233b-3ee9-4f14`** — the origin ticket this
bug attributes site 1 to. `_build-and-test.yml` documents the if-present guard for exactly this
skew; the new step did not copy it. The bug I am fixing and the gate that failed my fix for it
are the same defect, one layer apart.

### Mine: a bare `_child_diag` import that cannot survive a nested pytest run

Four pytest jobs, two tests, one cause:

```
ImportError: Error importing plugin "tests.interfaces.facades.test_cli": No module named '_child_diag'
```

`tests/unit/test_fixture_env_repr_security.py` lists `tests.interfaces.facades.test_cli` in
`_FIXTURE_SURFACES` and loads it as a `pytest_plugins` entry in a NESTED pytest run whose test
file lives in a tmp basetemp OUTSIDE `tests/`. There the root `tests/conftest.py` never loads,
so the `sys.path` injection every bare `from _child_diag import …` depends on never happens.

**I predicted this and under-weighted it.** The residual-risk note on the previous comment says
the bare import "resolves only because the root `tests/conftest.py` puts `tests/` on
`sys.path`", and I had already hit that exact `ModuleNotFoundError` in a scratch probe. I
dispositioned it "matched the repo's existing pattern" without checking whether any consumer
loads these modules outside that context. One does.

Fixed with the explicit `sys.path` bootstrap the `0e1d` precedent
(`tests/unit/test_live_dc_pass_health.py`) already uses, applied to all five site files.
Import robustness only — no assertion added, removed, or weakened. Still **0 deletions**.

## The finding that outlasts this ticket

I reported "full suite green, 11950 passed" and pushed on it. That log had an mtime **five
hours older than my change**: a stale file from a previous session. My own sweep never
finished, so the second never started, and I read a leftover and called it mine.

> **A log that says "passed" is indistinguishable from a log that says "passed" about
> different code.**

That is the same shape as the bug this ticket is about, and it happened FIVE times in this
session's own instruments — a colorized `grep "^FAILED"` that reported zero failures
unconditionally; a truncated sweep log identical to a clean one; an orphaned subshell reported
as finished; a `pgrep -f "make test"` that matched the monitor's own command line and waited on
itself; and the stale log above. Every one was caught only by checking the instrument against a
known-positive case. The first would have shipped a change claiming a clean kill matrix I had
never actually measured.

> **If you are verifying an absence, verify your instrument can still see a presence.**

Generalised as a review criterion in story `sphinxian-agrarian-snake`: ask of any check —
*can this produce its passing result for any reason other than the condition it claims to
verify?*

## Verification for patchset 2

Full suite green on the exact committed tree, and this time provably so: a freshly created
log that records the sha it started on (matching `HEAD`), an explicit `END` sentinel, and a
captured exit code — `EXITCODE=0`, **15209 passed, 55 skipped, 297 deselected, 1 xfailed**.
Rebased onto current `origin/main`; targeted re-check after the rebase 102 passed / 1 skipped;
`make lint` clean with the ratchet at `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`; `make typecheck` clean.

compiled_state.description:
## The defect

Two test sites outside the live-DC tier are the same **fail-OPEN** class as bug
`0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e` / `f0fb-de7a-b315-4508`, under a different phrasing. Each spawns a REAL
child with `subprocess.run`, never asserts a returncode, and its ONLY assertion is that some
string is ABSENT from the captured output. A child killed by a signal writes nothing, so the
absent-string assertion is trivially satisfied and the test reports GREEN for a run that never
executed.

Proven mechanism (bug `0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e`, 4/4 deterministic): a child that SIGKILLs itself
yields `returncode == -9` with `stdout == stderr == ""`.

### Site 1 — `tests/unit/test_git_floor_gate_tree_skew.py:127`

`test_absent_floor_file_emits_no_workflow_error`. `_run_gate` (line ~54) is
`subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", gate_script], capture_output=True)` with no `check=True` and no
returncode assertion. The whole test body is three lines and its only assertion is:

    assert "::error::" not in (result.stdout + result.stderr)

A reaped or OOM-killed bash child gives empty streams, so the gate script never ran and the test
still passes. This is a **success/health oracle** — the dangerous direction.

### Site 2 — `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py:151`

`test_reconcile_is_routed_...` (the non-integration one). Real child via `_cli(...)`. No
returncode assertion anywhere in the test; the sole assertion is:

    assert "unknown subcommand 'reconcile'" not in (cp.stdout + cp.stderr).lower()

Empty output from a signal-killed child satisfies it, so a never-started CLI reads as "the
dispatcher routed correctly".

### Borderline (lower risk, worth a look)

`tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py:243` — `_run_redispatch` asserts
`completed.returncode != 0`, which a `-9` / `137` exit ALSO satisfies, so the returncode check
does not fully close the gap. It is a message-quality oracle on a deliberately-failing run, so
the residual risk is low, but `!= 0` is the wrong shape for the same reason.

## Why it was not fixed in scope

Filed rather than fixed because both files sit outside the file lane of
`0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e` (the live-DC test files plus their shared helper) and were held by other
sessions at the time. They are also a different construct — an absent-string oracle over
`stdout + stderr`, not the `assert "Traceback" not in cp.stderr` shape — so folding them in
would have widened that change past what one review can carry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Neither site can pass on a signal-killed child: the returncode is asserted, not only the
      absence of a string in the captured output.
- [ ] A RED test proves it for each site — the child forced to die on a signal (empty output)
      makes the assertion fail before the fix, and the failure names the signal after it.
- [ ] `test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py:243`'s `returncode != 0` is tightened or explicitly
      justified, since a signal kill satisfies `!= 0`.
- [ ] Reuse `tests/_child_diag.py` (`child_failure_detail` / `assert_child_ran_clean`) rather
      than re-deriving the message, so every tier fails identically.

file_impact.reason: add assert_child_was_not_signal_killed, the narrow sibling of assert_child_ran_clean; message delegated to child_failure_detail so no tier re-derives the signal wording
site 1: guard the absent-::error:: skip oracle
site 2: guard the absent-unknown-subcommand routing oracle
site 3: guard the absent-::warning:: oracle whose returncode != 0 accepts a signal kill; justify the sibling that needs no guard
site 4 (Step-7 construct sweep): guard the absent-{color: pandoc oracle
site 5 (Step-7 construct sweep): guard the actionlint fail-fast oracle whose three assertions a killed child all satisfies
new regression test: drives all five real test bodies with a really-SIGKILLed child, plus a negative control proving the kill

compiled_state.title: Absent-string child oracles fail OPEN on a signal-killed child
